decided.claim: The substance signal is a top-level `panes` pane count (Option<usize>, skip-if-none) recorded in StateFile on every save from pane_count(); a count rather than a boolean or tab count, matching the existing count_saved_leaves richness metric and keeping threshold policy in the scanner.
Ranking gains one tier between the untouched workspace hint and recency: an arranged session (panes > 1) still in play outranks a scratch-sized one; within a tier, recency then id decide as before.

"Still in play" is measured save-to-save — within SUBSTANCE_WINDOW of the newest candidate's mtime, never of the launch clock — so a month away from the machine reorders nothing and the ordering is a stable fact about the saves.
SUBSTANCE_WINDOW is 7 days: a weekend of one-command windows cannot orphan Friday's wall, while 'abandoned weeks ago' always falls outside.

Compatibility: a file with no `panes` key ranks as arranged (is_none_or(n > 1)), so on the first launch after upgrading every pre-upgrade session orders exactly as today and is never demoted behind a fresh trivial one.

The scan stays one read_to_string per file: a hand-rolled toml_top_level_integer pulls `panes` from the same body the workspace hint already reads, stopping at the first table header; no session file is deserialised.
The scratch-window theme borrow (resolve_key/theme_key_in) shares the amended rank rather than keeping bare recency, so a tear-off inherits the wall's look and there is exactly one ordering.
The coupling between toml 0.8's serializer and the hand-rolled scanner is pinned by a test asserting `panes` and `last_workspace` land ahead of the first `[` table header in the serialized state.

least_confident.why: The ticket only bounds the window between a same-day throwaway and 'weeks'; 7 days is a judgment call with no empirical basis, and a different constant inside that range is equally defensible.

Relative-to-newest means an arranged session within the window of a months-old trivial newest still wins; I judged that correct (the throwaway story, frozen in time) but it is the semantics most open to argument versus clock-relative decay.
Changing the theme-borrow ordering is a side effect of sharing rank; keeping bare recency there would have preserved existing tear-off behaviour at the cost of two orderings.

not_done.claim: No backfill of pane counts into existing session files on upgrade; absence simply ranks as arranged until the session's next real save writes the count.
not_done.why: A migration would deserialise every session at boot — exactly what the ticket forbids — and the absent-means-arranged rule already gives the compatible ordering.
